correctness_confidence.basis: The signed discrepancy and three-number rounding bound agree with the primary tables. The marginal-error test inverts a bound for each candidate ratio and admits r=1. Two separate regressions at distinct horizons support the stated limited interpretation.

rigor.basis: The paper quantifies worst-case covariance and rounding separately. The normal approximation and common-operator assumption are explicit. No cluster-level sampling data were used to test finite-sample coverage.

novelty.basis: The regression consistency diagnostic and CAPEX-specific implications are a distinct application to a named source. Fieller inversion and the worst-case variance bound have explicit antecedents.

significance.basis: Readers gain a reproducible reason to distinguish the reported direction of reallocation from the share recovered. The analysis addresses one empirical paper and does not change a policy estimate using microdata.

reproducibility.basis: Two builds matched byte for byte and all three final pages were read. Numerical results from the pinned scripts matched the archived results in the PDF build. Table extraction depends on publisher layout and the original underlying firm-level regressions were not re-estimated.

summary: Working-paper assessment of the exact three-page PDF. The baseline ratio and two-horizon CAPEX contrast answer distinct questions. Three control discrepancies exceed 0.015. In the dynamic table the two component discrepancies are -0.20 and +0.06. Allowing unknown covariance admits full baseline offset and either sign for the sum of CAPEX coefficients. I participated in analysis and drafting in the same chat. This is an involved-model assessment, without independent replication of the underlying economic data.
strengths: Explicit falsifiable restriction on all common-design regression coefficients; the headline regressor alone passes it.
Two different normalizations and the timing of controls are central to the interpretation and correctly distinguished.
weaknesses: A single-paper audit does not establish how often reporting differences of this size occur or which data transformation caused them.
A future revision would benefit from reporting the numerical cross-horizon correlation threshold and a cluster-count sensitivity beside the asymptotic interval.
potential_errors: The term full compensation could be read as a causal project-level quantity if the abstract is read in isolation. Sections 2 and 4 limit it to a coefficient comparison.
Worst-case covariance sets admit singular joint limits. The actual panel structure may restrict this set and tighten inference; the reported intervals are conservative.
strong_novelty_candidates: The linked baseline and two-horizon additivity failures and the reduced-form inference obtained when covariance cannot be reconstructed from the total.
